sections.heading: 1. τὸ θηλυκόν ὄνομα (feminine noun) — 1st & 2nd declension
sections.content: Several feminine nouns appear here. ἡ σελήνη, ἡ θύρα, ἡ τράπεζα, ἡ καθέδρα, ἡ κλίνη, ἡ σκοτία follow the 1st declension. ἡ ὁδός is feminine but follows the 2nd-declension pattern (like ῥάβδος).

examples.greek: ἡ σελήνη ἀνατέλλει ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ
examples.note: 1st-decl. nominative
1st-decl. accusative

headingTranslations.fil: 1. Mga bagong pambabae na pangngalan (1st at 2nd declension)

sections.heading: 2. ἡ προθέσις ἐπί (preposition ἐπί) — three cases, three meanings
sections.content: ἐπί is one preposition with three meanings depending on case. With the genitive it means location on a surface; with the dative it means resting upon (already seen); with the accusative it means motion onto.

table.caption: ἡ προθέσις ἐπί (preposition ἐπί) — with three cases

examples.greek: εὑρίσκει τὸν λύχνον ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης
examples.note: gen.: he finds the lamp on the table
acc.: he sits down onto the chair

headingTranslations.es: 2. La preposición ἐπί — tres casos, tres significados
headingTranslations.pl: 2. Przyimek ἐπί — trzy przypadki, trzy znaczenia
headingTranslations.fil: 2. Ang preposisyon ἐπί — tatlong kaso, tatlong kahulugan

sections.heading: 3. τὸ ἐπίθετον (adjective) — agreement with feminine nouns
sections.content: When the noun is feminine, the adjective takes its feminine ending: -η / -α (nom.), -ην / -αν (acc.).

examples.note: the evening is beautiful
he has the beautiful bed

headingTranslations.es: 3. Concordancia del adjetivo con sustantivos femeninos
headingTranslations.fil: 3. Pagkakaayon ng pang-uri sa mga pambabae na pangngalan

contentTranslations.es: Cuando el sustantivo es femenino, el adjetivo toma su forma femenina: -η o -α (nominativo), -ην o -αν (acusativo).
contentTranslations.pl: Gdy rzeczownik jest żeński, przymiotnik przyjmuje żeńską formę: -η lub -α (mianownik), -ην lub -αν (biernik).
contentTranslations.fil: Kapag ang pangngalan ay pambabae, ang pang-uri ay kumukuha ng pambabae na anyo: -η o -α (nominative), -ην o -αν (accusative).

sections.heading: 4. ἡ αἰτιατική χρόνου (accusative of time duration)
sections.content: An accusative without a preposition can express how long an action lasts.

examples.note: he digs the field for a long time
it runs the whole day

headingTranslations.es: 4. El acusativo de duración de tiempo
headingTranslations.fil: 4. Ang accusative ng tagal ng oras

contentTranslations.es: Un acusativo sin preposición puede expresar cuánto tiempo dura una acción.
contentTranslations.pl: Biernik bez przyimka może wyrażać, jak długo trwa czynność.
contentTranslations.fil: Ang accusative nang walang preposisyon ay maaaring magpahayag ng gaano katagal ang isang kilos.

sections.heading: 5. τὸ ἐπίρρημα (adverb) — formation and common forms
sections.content: Adjectives often form adverbs by replacing -ος with -ως (e.g. καλός > καλῶς). Other useful adverbs: ἔτι, οὐκέτι, σφόδρα.

examples.note: the river flows well

examples.greek: ὁ λύχνος ἔτι λάμπει· οὐκέτι σκοτία ἐστίν
examples.note: the lamp still shines; it is no longer dark

headingTranslations.es: 5. El adverbio — formación y formas comunes
headingTranslations.fil: 5. Ang pang-abay — pagbuo at mga karaniwang anyo

contentTranslations.es: Los adjetivos forman adverbios reemplazando -ος con -ως (ej. καλός → καλῶς). Otros adverbios: ἔτι (aún), οὐκέτι (ya no), σφόδρα (muy).
contentTranslations.pl: Przymiotniki tworzą przysłówki przez zastąpienie -ος przez -ως (np. καλός → καλῶς). Inne przysłówki: ἔτι (jeszcze), οὐκέτι (już nie), σφόδρα (bardzo).
contentTranslations.fil: Ang mga pang-uri ay bumubuo ng pang-abay sa pamamagitan ng pagpapalit ng -ος ng -ως (hal. καλός → καλῶς). Iba pang pang-abay: ἔτι (pa rin), οὐκέτι (hindi na), σφόδρα (napaka).

sections.heading: 6. ὁ ἀπαρέμφατος (infinitive) — chains with καί
sections.content: A single verb of wanting can govern several infinitives joined by καί.

examples.greek: θέλει ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν καὶ ἡσυχάζειν
examples.note: he wants to eat and drink and rest

examples.greek: οὐ θέλει ἔτι καθίζειν καὶ μένειν
examples.note: he no longer wants to sit and stay

headingTranslations.fil: 6. Ang infinitive — mga hanay na may καί

sections.heading: 1. τὸ ἄρθρον (article) — full chart, all numbers and genders
sections.content: This part shows plurals in many cases and genders for the first time. The article forms: οἱ / αἱ / τά (nom. pl.), τούς / τάς / τά (acc. pl.), τῶν (gen. pl. — same for all genders), τοῖς / ταῖς / τοῖς (dat. pl.).

tables.caption: τὸ ἄρθρον (article) — full chart, all numbers and genders
τὸ ὄνομα (noun) — full endings, all genders

examples.greek: οὐ μία ἀλλὰ πολλαὶ θύραι εἰσιν
examples.note: fem. nom. pl.: there are not one but many doors

examples.greek: θέλει σῴζειν τὰ ζῷα ἀπὸ τῶν λύκων
examples.note: masc. gen. pl.: he wants to save the animals from the wolves

headingTranslations.es: 1. El artículo — cuadro completo, todos los números y géneros
headingTranslations.pl: 1. Rodzajnik — pełna tabela, wszystkie liczby i rodzaje
headingTranslations.fil: 1. Ang pantukoy — kumpletong tsart, lahat ng bilang at uri

sections.heading: 2. εἷς, μία, ἕν (numeral 'one') — all genders
sections.content: "One" has three genders. Ordinals (πρῶτος, δεύτερος, τρίτος) are regular -ος, -η, -ον adjectives.

examples.greek: οὐχ εἷς λίθος ἀλλὰ λίθοι πολλοί
examples.note: not one stone but many stones

examples.greek: ἀνοίγει τὴν πρώτην θύραν … τὴν δευτέραν … τὴν τρίτην
examples.note: he opens the first door … the second … the third

headingTranslations.es: 2. εἷς, μία, ἕν («uno») — todos los géneros
headingTranslations.fil: 2. εἷς, μία, ἕν («isa») — lahat ng uri

sections.heading: 3. τὸ ἐπίθετον πολύς (adjective πολύς) — irregular 'much, many'
sections.content: Like μέγας, πολύς uses two stems: πολυ- in the masc./neut. nom. sg., and πολλ- elsewhere.

examples.greek: λίθοι πολλοί εἰσιν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ
examples.note: masc. nom. pl.: there are many stones in the field
fem. nom. pl.: there are many doors

sections.heading: 4. ὁ ἐνεστὼς ἐνεργετικὴ ὁριστική (Present Active Indicative) — αʹ πληθυντικόν (1st plural)
sections.content: The 1st-plural ending is -ομεν. The pronoun ἡμεῖς ("we") is used for emphasis.

examples.note: we want to eat
we have neither fruits nor bread

headingTranslations.es: 4. Indicativo activo presente — 1ª persona del plural

sections.heading: 5. ὁ ἐνεστὼς ἐνεργετικὴ ὁριστική (Present Active Indicative) — βʹ ἑνικόν (2nd singular) full paradigm
sections.content: The 2nd-singular ending is -εις. For "to be," the form is εἶ. The pronoun σύ ("you") is emphatic.

table.caption: ὁ ἐνεστὼς ἐνεργετικὴ ὁριστική (Present Active Indicative) — full paradigm

examples.note: you are righteous and faithful

examples.greek: σὺ σῴζεις αὐτὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ λύκου
examples.note: you save it from the wolf

headingTranslations.es: 5. Indicativo activo presente — 2ª persona del singular, paradigma completo
headingTranslations.pl: 5. Czas teraźniejszy czynny — 2. os. l.poj., pełny paradygmat
headingTranslations.fil: 5. Present active indicative — 2nd singular, kumpletong paradigma

sections.heading: 6. τὸ ἀντώνυμον (pronoun) — ἐγώ and σύ, all cases
sections.content: The 1st- and 2nd-person pronouns have full case forms. They are usually omitted (the verb already shows the person), and when used they are emphatic.

table.caption: τὸ ἀντώνυμον (pronoun) — ἐγώ / ἡμεῖς and σύ

examples.note: you love me
I give thanks to you

headingTranslations.es: 6. Los pronombres personales ἐγώ y σύ
headingTranslations.fil: 6. Mga personal pronoun ἐγώ at σύ

sections.heading: 7. οὐ δυνατόν ἐστιν — impersonal expression with dative + infinitive
sections.content: An impersonal expression: "it is (not) possible (for X) to do (Y)." The dative names the person; the infinitive names the action.

examples.greek: οὐ δυνατόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ αἴρειν πάντας τοὺς λίθους
examples.note: it is not possible for him to lift all the stones

examples.greek: οὐ δυνατόν ἐστιν εὑρίσκειν τὸν λύχνον
examples.note: it is not possible to find the lamp

headingTranslations.es: 7. οὐ δυνατόν ἐστιν — expresión impersonal con dativo + infinitivo
headingTranslations.pl: 7. οὐ δυνατόν ἐστιν — wyrażenie bezosobowe z celownikiem + bezokolicznik
headingTranslations.fil: 7. οὐ δυνατόν ἐστιν — impersonal na pahayag na may dative + infinitive

sections.heading: 8. τὸ ἐρωτηματικόν (interrogative) — τί (what?) and ποῦ (where?)
sections.content: τί is the interrogative pronoun "what?"; ποῦ is the interrogative adverb "where?" Both can also introduce indirect questions.

examples.note: direct: what are you saying?

examples.greek: οὐ γινώσκει τί ποιεῖ· ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ ἀρνίον;
examples.note: he doesn't know what he is doing; where is the lamb?

sections.heading: 9. τὸ ἐπίθετον πᾶς (adjective πᾶς) — all, every
sections.content: πᾶς in the singular often means "every" (each one); in the plural, "all." Like μέγας, it has irregular forms.

examples.note: masc. acc. pl.: all the stones
masc. nom. sg.: every person

headingTranslations.es: 9. El adjetivo πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν («todo, cada»)
headingTranslations.fil: 9. Ang pang-uri πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν («lahat, bawat»)
